# QS-PROC-06 Forging temperature control (P2)
Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-IH02

Scope
- This quality specification defines mandatory requirements and inspection methods for forging temperature control related to Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) on line P2-L1 at Plant P2. It applies to operations, maintenance, and quality personnel responsible for set up, monitoring, and corrective action for induction heating and associated coil cooling systems. Refer to change control and operating procedures listed in References.

Background and rationale
- Consistent temperature control of billets during induction heating is critical to forging quality and die life. Induction heater coil cooling directly affects heater performance and reliability. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. Maintaining this minimum prevents coil overheating, reduces risk of equipment damage, and stabilizes heat transfer to the billet. This specification implements a single-point requirement for coil cooling flow and defines inspection and nonconformance handling to ensure traceability and timely corrective action.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Responsibility |
|---|---:|---|
| Coil cooling water flow for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 | The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) is 55 L/min. | Production lead, Maintenance lead |
| Flow sensing and recording | Flow sensing devices must be functional and provide readable output to the operator interface; records of flow readings associated with each heating batch must be retained as specified in Records. | Instrumentation technician |
| Preventive maintenance interaction | Preventive maintenance activities that affect coil or water circuits must follow SOP-P2-L1-02 and SOP-P2-L1-03 and be documented in maintenance logs. | Maintenance planner |
| Change control | Any modification to heating or cooling circuits must be initiated via ECN-2026-039 or successor change notice processes and approved prior to implementation. | Engineering |

Inspection method
- Purpose: Verify that coil cooling flow meets the minimum requirement and that sensing/recording systems are competent for quality records.

- Pre-inspection check: Confirm continuity of the water circuit and that instrumentation is powered and communicating. If instrumentation is nonfunctional, follow nonconformance handling below; do not proceed without initiating corrective steps.

- Measurement: For each operational shift or production batch, observe the flow instrument associated with EQ-P2-L1-IH02 and confirm the recorded value meets the requirement. When automated logs are available, extract the flow record corresponding to the heating event and include it with the production run documentation.

- Acceptance decision: A flow record that meets the requirement is acceptable. A flow reading below the minimum is nonconforming; take immediate action per Nonconformance handling.

- Examples and rationale:
  - Example of acceptable record: an operator log entry or automated record indicating the flow at or above the minimum during the heating event. This validates cooling adequacy for that event.
  - Example of nonconforming record: any record showing flow below the minimum during a heating event, or missing flow data for a heating event where verification cannot be established. Missing data is treated equivalently to below-minimum flow for disposition purposes because it prevents verification of cooling adequacy.

- Records to keep: Retain the flow reading or automated log extract associated with each heating batch, the operator verification checklist, and any corrective action records generated for the event. These records support quality investigations and must be available for audits and for any ECN invoked.

Nonconformance handling
- Immediate actions:
  - If coil cooling flow for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is found below the minimum, stop billet feed to the heater and notify maintenance and production supervision immediately.
  - Isolate the heater per safe work practices and secure the process to prevent further heating events until documented corrective action is completed.

- Troubleshooting steps and documentation:
  - Verify instrument function and wiring. If instrumentation is failed, document failure and initiate repair under SOP-P2-L1-02 or SOP-P2-L1-03 as applicable.
  - Inspect supply circuits and valves for obvious restriction or isolation. Record findings in the maintenance log and in the unit incident report.

- Disposition and corrective action:
  - Do not release any forgings processed during intervals where coil cooling flow could not be verified as meeting the minimum, until an engineering disposition is issued.
  - Document corrective actions taken, root cause analysis, and verification of restoration of compliant flow. Include flow records demonstrating sustained compliance before returning the heater to normal production.

- Escalation and change control:
  - If the root cause implicates design, materials, or recurring failures, initiate ECN-2026-039 to propose engineering changes. All modifications must be approved and documented before implementation.

Records and retention
- Maintain the following records linked to each heating event or batch: flow reading or automated log extract for EQ-P2-L1-IH02, operator verification checklist, maintenance incident reports, corrective action documentation, and any related ECN documentation. Retain records per the plant records retention policy and make available for quality audits.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-039
- SOP-P2-L1-02
- SOP-P2-L1-03

Revision control
- This specification is Rev E. Amendments to this document must be processed through the plant document control workflow and cross-referenced to ECN-2026-039 when applicable.
